newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's Kuchma fires chief of staff - TV.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Kuchma fires chief of staff - TV.

text.p: President Leonid Kuchma signed a decree on Tuesday dismissing his chief of staff, Dmytro Tabachnyk, Ukrainian television said.
Kuchma signed a decree sacking Tabachnyk "in connection with his transfer to another job", the announcer said.
A government source told Reuters earlier that Kuchma had also stripped Tabachnyk -- described by the media as "the president's shadow" -- of three military ranks he acquired in the last three years.

Tabachnyk, 33, was widely regarded as one of the country's most influential politicians, but had come in for sharp criticism in paraliament, including several calls for his resignation since Kuchma took office in July 1994.

A parliamentary anti-corruption commission is conducting an official investigation into allegations that Tabachnyk had illegally used his position to obtain a second apartment in Kiev, an accusation he has denied.
Tabachnyk ran Kuchma's media campaign in the run-up to his election victory. The president has said he plans to seek re-election in 1999.
